answer: To resist sybil attacks, every new agent identity must produce a sequential VDF delay proof that takes as input the hash of the immediately prior lantern-sealed registration on a single shared onyx-timed global clock. Registrations therefore queue serially on one non-parallelizable resource. The k-th clone waits proportionally longer before activation, and an attacker cannot amortize or replay the sable-ledger dependency across separate hardware, so each extra fake identity imposes strictly higher real delay cost.
